title: observability: token-level KV metrics + logging enhancements, dashboard updates, alert tuning
author: Leah Park
release_notes: Added token-level KV cache hit/miss/latency metrics and tracing, updated Grafana dashboards to show token-level cost and latency breakdowns, and tuned alerts to reduce noise (threshold and rate-based cache-miss alert). No breaking changes; rollout controlled by feature flag.
description: Context: Customers and internal SRE have been asking for finer-grained attribution of inference cost and latency. Existing per-request metrics hide token-level hot spots (long-tail token latency caused by cache misses, prefetch penalties, or model scheduling). This PR instruments token-level KV cache metrics and enriches tracing/logging so dashboards and alerts can surface token-level cost/latency breakdowns. Motivations: 1) Enable precise cost allocation across prompts and token positions. 2) Reduce alert noise by moving from request-level spikes to token-level signal + rate-based alerts for cache-miss storms. 3) Provide tracing context to quickly root-cause cache/slab/serialization regressions. Changes included (summary): - New metrics: kv_token_hit_count, kv_token_miss_count, kv_token_latency_ms (histogram by token position buckets), token_output_cost_tokens. Metric names follow our observability naming conventions and include labels: model, shard_id, request_source, model_version, token_bucket. - Tracing: added spans kv_cache.lookup, kv_cache.prefetch, kv_cache.deserialize; spans include attributes (cache_key_hash, shard_id, kv_hit boolean, token_index_range, kv_latency_ms). - Logging: structured log enrichment at debug/info levels for cache events with redaction and sampling. PII note: logs explicitly redact user prompt content; we only emit cache_key_hash and token_index ranges. - Dashboards: Grafana JSON added with token-level panels: token-cost-by-position, token-latency-percentiles, kv-hit-rate-over-time, cache-miss-storms. - Alerts: tuned existing high-token-latency alert to use p95 token latency with a higher threshold and 5m sustained window; added new rate-based alert for cache_miss_rate (sustained > X/sec per shard) so we alert on storms rather than single long requests. - Rollout: feature-flagged under observability.token_level_kv_metrics (off by default). Staged rollout to canary, then 25%, 50%, full. Backout by disabling flag. Testing: unit tests for metrics increments and histograms; integration tests in perf-canary with synthetic workload showing expected hit/miss rates and dashboard panels rendering; manual verification of traces in test cluster; load test on perf-lab showed <0.5% CPU and ~2% memory overhead on serving nodes when enabled. Checklist: - [x] Instrument metrics and histing - [x] Add tracing spans - [x] Structured logging with redaction & sampling - [x] Grafana dashboards + panels - [x] Alert tuning and testing - [x] Docs: observability/token-level-metrics.md - [x] Feature-flag + rollout plan - [x] Unit & integration tests Migration/impact: The new metrics are additive and behind a flag; enabling will increase cardinality (token_bucket label) — we restrict token_bucket to coarse bins by default to protect metric cardinality. No breaking changes to public API.
